recipes.name: Palak Paneer with Brown Rice Roti
recipes.health_benefit: This dish is rich in iron from spinach, calcium from paneer, and fiber from spinach and whole wheat roti, which supports hemoglobin levels and bone health, and helps manage blood sugar and cholesterol.
instructions: Blanch spinach for 2-3 minutes, then immediately plunge into ice water. Drain and blend to a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds. Once they splutter, add chopped onion and sauté until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili, cook for 1 minute. Add chopped tomato and cook until soft.
Add turmeric, coriander, and garam masala powders. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add spinach paste and salt, mix well. Bring to a simmer.
Cut paneer into cubes and add to the gravy. Cook for 5-7 minutes.
For rotis, combine whole wheat and brown rice flour with salt. Knead into a soft dough using water.
Roll out small portions into thin rotis and cook on a hot tawa until puffed and cooked through.
Serve Palak Paneer hot with Brown Rice Roti.

recipes.name: Grilled Fish with Steamed Greens
recipes.health_benefit: This meal is an excellent source of Omega-3 fatty acids and Vitamin D from fish, which are crucial for cardiovascular health, supporting healthy HDL and triglyceride levels. Lean protein aids satiety and muscle maintenance.
instructions: Marinate fish with lemon juice, garlic paste, ginger paste, turmeric, red chili powder, salt, and mustard oil for 15-20 minutes.
Preheat grill or non-stick pan to medium-high heat.
Grill the fish for 4-5 minutes per side, or until cooked through and flaky.
Steam broccoli and carrots until tender-crisp (about 5-7 minutes). Add spinach for the last minute.
Serve grilled fish immediately with the steamed greens.

recipes.name: Sprouted Moong Dal Chaat (Nut-Free)
recipes.health_benefit: This high-fiber, high-protein snack helps stabilize blood sugar levels, supports healthy digestion, and provides B vitamins and iron, contributing to overall metabolic health and energy.
instructions: Gently steam or blanch sprouted moong dal for 3-5 minutes until slightly tender but still crunchy. Drain well.
In a large bowl, combine the steamed moong dal, chopped cucumber, tomato, onion, pomegranate seeds, green chili (if using), and coriander leaves.
Add lemon juice, chaat masala, and black salt. Toss everything gently to combine.
Serve immediately as a refreshing and nutritious snack.

recipes.name: Chicken and Vegetable Pulao (Brown Rice)
recipes.health_benefit: A balanced meal providing lean protein from chicken and complex carbohydrates from brown rice for sustained energy. The vegetables add fiber and micronutrients, supporting overall metabolic health and satiety.
instructions: Rinse brown rice thoroughly and soak for 30 minutes. Drain.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or pressure cooker. Add cumin seeds, bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods. Sauté for a minute.
Add sliced onion and cook until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for 2 minutes.
Add diced chicken and cook until it changes color.
Stir in turmeric powder, coriander powder, and garam masala. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add mixed vegetables and soaked brown rice. Sauté gently for 2 minutes.
Pour in water and add salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and cook until rice is done and water is absorbed (about 20-25 minutes in a pot, 2-3 whistles in a pressure cooker).
Let it rest for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork. Garnish with fresh coriander.
Serve hot with raita or plain yogurt.

recipes.name: Egg Bhurji with Whole Wheat Toast
recipes.health_benefit: This breakfast provides excellent lean protein from eggs for muscle health and satiety. Eggs are also a good source of Vitamin B12 and Vitamin D, which are important for energy metabolism and overall well-being.
instructions: Whisk eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper in a bowl.
Heat mustard oil in a non-stick pan. Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent.
Add grated ginger and green chili (if using), cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomato and cook until soft and slightly pulpy.
Stir in turmeric powder and red chili powder. Cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in the whisked eggs and scramble gently until cooked but still moist.
Stir in fresh coriander leaves.
Toast the whole wheat bread slices.
Serve Egg Bhurji hot with whole wheat toast.

recipes.name: Ragi Dosa with Coconut Chutney (Nut-Free)
recipes.health_benefit: Ragi (finger millet) is an excellent source of calcium and dietary fiber, important for bone density and blood sugar management. This provides a healthy, gluten-free option that contributes to calcium intake.
instructions: Grind soaked urad dal and fenugreek seeds with a little water to a smooth batter. Mix with ragi flour, rice flour, and salt. Add water to make a dosa consistency batter. Ferment overnight (8-10 hours).
To make chutney: Blend grated coconut, green chilies, and ginger with a little water to a smooth paste. Add salt to taste.
For chutney tempering: Heat 1 tsp oil, add mustard seeds, and urad dal. Once seeds splutter and dal turns golden, add curry leaves. Pour over the chutney.
Heat a non-stick tawa. Pour a ladleful of dosa batter and spread thinly in a circular motion.
Drizzle a little mustard oil around the edges. Cook until golden brown and crisp.
Fold and serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.
